subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Capital Grant Presentation Options
question: GreenEnergy Ltd. receives a Government Grant of ₹20 Crores towards the purchase of a pollution control plant costing ₹100 Crores (useful life 10 years, residual value nil). Under Ind AS 20, what are the two permissible methods of presenting this grant on the balance sheet?
options: Option 1: Credit directly to Equity Share Capital; Option 2: Recognize as immediate revenue in P&L.

Option 1: Present the grant as Deferred Income (which is recognized in profit or loss on a systematic basis over the 10-year useful life of the plant); Option 2: Deduct the grant in arriving at the carrying amount of the asset (reducing initial plant cost to ₹80 Crores, depreciated at ₹8 Crores/year).
Option 1: Credit to Revaluation Reserve; Option 2: Treat as an off-balance sheet item.
Government grants for capital assets cannot be recognized under Ind AS.
ref: Ind AS 20 (Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance) - Paragraph 24: Grants Related to Assets
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 24 provides two methods of presenting grants related to assets in the balance sheet: (a) setting up the grant as deferred income, which is recognized in profit or loss on a systematic basis over the useful life of the asset; or (b) deducting the grant in calculating the carrying amount of the asset (depreciation is charged on the reduced carrying amount).

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Below-Market Interest Rate Government Loans
question: On 1st April 2023, BioPharma Ltd. receives an interest-free loan of ₹10 Crores from the Department of Biotechnology repayable in full after 5 years. The market borrowing rate for an equivalent commercial loan is 10% per annum (PV factor for 5 years at 10% = 0.6209). How should this loan and government assistance be recorded on 1st April 2023 under Ind AS 109 and Ind AS 20?
options: Record loan liability at full ₹10 Crores with zero government grant recognition.

Measure the financial liability at fair value of ₹6.209 Crores under Ind AS 109; the difference of ₹3.791 Crores between initial cash proceeds and fair value is recognized as a Government Grant (Deferred Income) under Ind AS 20 to be recognized in profit or loss over the period of the loan.
Recognize ₹3.791 Crores immediately as an exceptional gain in P&L.
Record the loan in Other Comprehensive Income.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 10A & Ind AS 109: Below-Market Government Loans
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 10A states: 'The benefit of a government loan at a below-market rate of interest is treated as a government grant. The loan shall be recognized and measured in accordance with Ind AS 109. The benefit of the below-market rate of interest shall be measured as the difference between the initial carrying value of the loan determined in accordance with Ind AS 109 and the proceeds received.' The ₹3.791 Cr benefit is accounted for under Ind AS 20.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Repayment of Government Grants
question: Four years ago, Apex Textiles received a government grant of ₹5 Crores towards a factory facility, which was accounted for by deducting the grant from the asset carrying amount. In FY 2023-24, due to a breach of employment covenants, the Government demanded full repayment of the ₹5 Crores grant. How should this repayment be accounted for under Ind AS 20?
options: Recognize full ₹5 Crores as an extraordinary prior period error.

Repayment of a grant related to an asset shall be recognized by increasing the carrying amount of the asset; the cumulative additional depreciation that would have been recognized in profit or loss to date in the absence of the grant shall be recognized immediately in profit or loss.
Deducted directly from retained earnings.
Treated as an expense in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 32: Repayment of Grants Related to an Asset
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 32 states: 'Repayment of a grant related to an asset shall be recognized by increasing the carrying amount of the asset or reducing the deferred income balance by the amount repayable. The cumulative additional depreciation that would have been recognized in profit or loss to date in the absence of the grant shall be recognized immediately in profit or loss.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Grant Given as Immediate Financial Support for Past Losses
question: During an economic crisis, the State Government issues an unconditional cash grant of ₹10 Crores to AgroMills Ltd. to provide immediate financial relief for severe drought losses incurred in the preceding agricultural season. Under Ind AS 20, how should this grant be recognized?
options: Deferred and recognized over the next 5 years.
Recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss of the period in which it becomes receivable as an item of income, because it was given as immediate financial support with no future related costs.
Credited directly to Capital Reserve in Equity.
Recognized in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 20: Grant as Immediate Financial Relief
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 20 states: 'A government grant that becomes receivable as compensation for expenses or losses already incurred or for the purpose of giving immediate financial support to the entity with no future related costs shall be recognized in profit or loss of the period in which it becomes receivable.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Definition of a Qualifying Asset
question: Which of the following assets qualifies as a 'Qualifying Asset' eligible for capitalization of borrowing costs under Ind AS 23?
options: Inventories that are routinely manufactured or produced in large quantities on a repetitive basis over a few hours.

An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale (such as a toll bridge taking 3 years to construct or aging single-malt whiskey requiring 12 years of maturation).
Financial assets measured at fair value under Ind AS 109.
Assets that are ready for their intended use or sale when acquired.
ref: Ind AS 23 (Borrowing Costs) - Paragraph 5: Definition of Qualifying Asset
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 5 defines a qualifying asset as 'an asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale.' Examples include manufacturing plants, power generation facilities, intangible assets under development, and investment properties under construction. Financial assets and inventories produced over a short period are explicitly excluded.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Commencement of Capitalisation Criteria
question: Which three criteria must ALL be satisfied simultaneously for an entity to commence capitalising borrowing costs as part of the cost of a qualifying asset under Ind AS 23?
options: Loan agreement signed, bank disburses funds, and interest is paid.
(a) It incurs expenditures for the asset; (b) it incurs borrowing costs; and (c) it undertakes activities that are necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale.
Board passes a resolution, architectural drawings are finalized, and building permits are applied for.
Statutory auditor inspects the construction site.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraph 17: Commencement of Capitalisation
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 17 specifies: 'An entity shall begin capitalising borrowing costs as part of the cost of a qualifying asset on the commencement date. The commencement date for capitalisation is the date when the entity first meets all of the following conditions: (a) it incurs expenditures for the asset; (b) it incurs borrowing costs; and (c) it undertakes activities that are necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Temporary Investment Income on Specific Borrowings
question: InfraCorp Ltd. borrows ₹50 Crores specifically to construct a marine drydock on 1st April 2023 at 10% interest. Construction begins immediately. During the first 6 months, ₹20 Crores of surplus borrowed funds not yet needed for site payments were temporarily invested in money market mutual funds, earning interest income of ₹80 Lakhs. What is the net borrowing cost capitalized for the year ended 31st March 2024?
options: ₹5.0 Crores (gross interest of 10% on ₹50 Crores), with ₹80 Lakhs recognized as finance income in P&L.
₹4.2 Crores (Gross borrowing costs incurred of ₹5.0 Crores minus temporary investment income earned of ₹80 Lakhs on specific borrowings).
Zero, because borrowing costs on specific borrowings cannot be capitalized.
₹5.8 Crores.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraph 12: Specific Borrowings & Temporary Investment Income
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 12 states: 'To the extent that an entity borrows funds specifically for the purpose of obtaining a qualifying asset, the entity shall determine the amount of borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation as the actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing during the period less any investment income on the temporary investment of those borrowings.' Eligible = ₹5.0 Cr - ₹0.8 Cr = ₹4.2 Crores.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Capitalisation Rate for General Borrowings
question: Titan Ltd. incurs capital expenditure of ₹40 Crores on a qualifying asset during the year, financed through general corporate borrowings. Its general borrowing pool consists of: (i) ₹60 Crores bank loan at 8% p.a. (interest ₹4.8 Cr); and (ii) ₹40 Crores debentures at 10% p.a. (interest ₹4.0 Cr). What is the weighted average capitalization rate and borrowing cost capitalized for the year under Ind AS 23?
options: Rate = 9.0%; Borrowing cost capitalized = ₹3.6 Crores.
Rate = 8.8% (Total interest ₹8.8 Crores / Total general borrowings ₹100 Crores); Borrowing cost capitalized = 8.8% × ₹40 Crores = ₹3.52 Crores.
Rate = 10%; Borrowing cost capitalized = ₹4.0 Crores.
Rate = 8%; Borrowing cost capitalized = ₹3.2 Crores.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraph 14: Capitalisation Rate on General Borrowings
explanation: Under Ind AS 23 Paragraph 14, the capitalization rate shall be the weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to all borrowings of the entity that are outstanding during the period, other than borrowings made specifically for the purpose of obtaining a qualifying asset. Capitalization rate = ₹8.8 Cr / ₹100 Cr = 8.8%. Capitalized borrowing cost = ₹40 Cr × 8.8% = ₹3.52 Crores.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Suspension of Capitalisation During Extended Interruption
question: Construction of a hydroelectric dam is halted for 6 months due to a violent local labor strike and environmental litigation (abnormal stoppage not necessary for the engineering process). How should the borrowing costs incurred during this 6-month idle period be treated under Ind AS 23?
options: Continue capitalising borrowing costs without interruption.

An entity shall suspend capitalisation of borrowing costs during extended periods in which it suspends active development of a qualifying asset; borrowing costs incurred during the 6 months are expensed in Profit or Loss.
Capitalize 50% and expense 50%.
Recognize in OCI.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraphs 20-21: Suspension of Capitalisation
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 20 states: 'An entity shall suspend capitalisation of borrowing costs during extended periods in which it suspends active development of a qualifying asset.' Paragraph 21 clarifies that capitalisation is not suspended when a temporary delay is a necessary part of the process of getting an asset ready (e.g. high water levels during rainy season in bridge building), but strikes and disputes require suspension.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Cessation of Capitalisation for Parts Completed in Stages
question: A commercial real estate park consists of 5 standalone office towers. Tower 1 is structurally finished, air-conditioned, licensed, and ready for commercial leasing on 31st December 2023, while Towers 2 to 5 are still under construction. Can borrowing costs continue to be capitalized on Tower 1 after 31st December 2023?
options: Yes, capitalization continues until all 5 towers of the entire business park are completed.

No, when an entity completes the construction of a qualifying asset in parts and each part is capable of being used while construction continues on other parts, the entity shall cease capitalising borrowing costs when it completes substantially all the activities necessary to prepare that part for its intended use or sale.
Capitalization ceases only when tenants sign lease deeds.
Borrowing costs on Tower 1 must be reversed retrospectively.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraph 24: Cessation of Capitalisation for Assets Completed in Parts
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 24 specifies: 'When an entity completes the construction of a qualifying asset in parts and each part is capable of being used while construction continues on other parts, the entity shall cease capitalising borrowing costs when it completes substantially all the activities necessary to prepare that part for its intended use or sale.' Capitalization on Tower 1 ceases on 31st December.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Non-Monetary Government Grants
question: The State Government allocates 50 acres of prime industrial land to GreenTech Ltd. free of cost to establish a semiconductor wafer fabrication plant. The nominal stamp registration fee paid was ₹10,000. The fair value of the land is appraised at ₹25 Crores by government approved valuers. Under Ind AS 20, how may GreenTech Ltd. account for this non-monetary government grant?
options: Only at the nominal value of ₹10,000.

Under Ind AS 20 Paragraph 23, the entity may account for both the asset and the grant either at the fair value of the non-monetary asset (₹25 Crores land with a corresponding ₹25 Crores deferred government grant) or at a nominal amount (₹10,000).
At ₹25 Crores with a credit to Share Capital.
Non-monetary grants cannot be recognized on the balance sheet.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 23: Non-Monetary Government Grants
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 23 states: 'A government grant may take the form of a transfer of a non-monetary asset, such as land or other resources, for the use of the entity. In these circumstances it is usual to assess the fair value of the non-monetary asset and to account for both grant and asset at that fair value. An alternative course that is sometimes followed is to record both asset and grant at a nominal amount.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Matching Principle for Grants Related to Income
question: SkillIndia Ltd. receives a Government Grant of ₹30 Lakhs in March 2024 to reimburse training costs for underprivileged apprentices. The training program will run across FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26 (training costs projected at ₹20 Lakhs in Year 1 and ₹40 Lakhs in Year 2). How should the grant be recognized in profit or loss under Ind AS 20?
options: Recognize entire ₹30 Lakhs as income in March 2024 when cash is received.

Recognized in profit or loss on a systematic basis over the periods in which the entity recognizes as expenses the related costs for which the grant is intended to compensate: ₹10 Lakhs in Year 1 (₹20L/₹60L × ₹30L) and ₹20 Lakhs in Year 2 (₹40L/₹60L × ₹30L).
Split equally at ₹15 Lakhs per year.
Credited directly to general reserve.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 12: Recognition of Grants Related to Income
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 12 states: 'Government grants shall be recognized in profit or loss on a systematic basis over the periods in which the entity recognizes as expenses the related costs for which the grants are intended to compensate.' The grant is recognized pro-rata to the incurred training costs.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Land Acquisition as Qualifying Asset
question: Urban Developers Ltd. purchases vacant freehold land for ₹100 Crores using bank borrowings. The land is intended to be held for long-term capital appreciation, with no active site development or construction planned in the foreseeable future. Are the borrowing costs on this land loan eligible for capitalization under Ind AS 23?
options: Yes, land is always a qualifying asset under Ind AS 23.

No, borrowing costs incurred on land acquired without any associated development activities are NOT eligible for capitalisation, because the land was ready for its intended use (holding for capital appreciation) when acquired and does not undergo activities necessary to prepare it for intended use.
Yes, up to 10% of land value.
Capitalized only if land is revalued.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraphs 5 & 19: Land without Development is Not a Qualifying Asset
explanation: Ind AS 23 states that an asset is a qualifying asset only if it takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use. Land acquired without development is ready for its intended use when acquired. However, land that is acquired for development (e.g. where substantial earthworks, roads, and utilities are being developed) qualifies while the development activities are ongoing.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Forgivable Loans
question: Under a rural industrialization scheme, the Government grants a loan of ₹2 Crores to SmallCrafts Ltd. The terms state that the loan will be forgiven in full if the company maintains continuous operations and employs at least 50 rural artisans for 3 consecutive years. Under Ind AS 20, how is a forgivable loan treated?
options: Treated as permanent equity from day 1.
A forgivable loan from government is treated as a government grant when there is reasonable assurance that the entity will meet the terms for forgiveness of the loan.
Accounted for as a contingent liability.
Ignored until the 3 years elapse.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 10: Forgivable Loans as Government Grants
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 10 states: 'A forgivable loan from government is treated as a government grant when there is reasonable assurance that the entity will meet the terms for forgiveness of the loan.' When reasonable assurance exists, it is accounted for as a grant.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Excess Carrying Amount of Qualifying Asset Over Recoverable Amount
question: When the carrying amount or the expected ultimate cost of a qualifying asset (including capitalized borrowing costs) exceeds its recoverable amount or net realizable value, what is the mandatory requirement under Ind AS 23?
options: Capitalization of borrowing costs must be increased to match fair value.
The carrying amount is written down or written off in accordance with the requirements of other Standards (such as Ind AS 36 Impairment of Assets or Ind AS 2 Inventories).
Borrowing costs are moved to Other Comprehensive Income.
Capitalization continues unaffected.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Paragraph 16: Impairment of Qualifying Assets
explanation: Ind AS 23 Paragraph 16 states: 'When the carrying amount or the expected ultimate cost of the qualifying asset exceeds its recoverable amount or net realizable value, the carrying amount is written down or written off in accordance with the requirements of other Standards. In certain circumstances, the amount of the write-down or write-off is written back in accordance with those other Standards.'

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Government Assistance without Quantifiable Value
question: The Ministry of Heavy Industries provides free technical advisory assistance and sanitary quarantine consultation to automotive exporters, but the service cannot reasonably have a value placed upon it. Under Ind AS 20, how should this government assistance be treated?
options: Valued at management's best estimate and recorded as revenue.
Excluded from financial values on the balance sheet and P&L, but disclosed in the notes to financial statements, specifying the nature, extent, and duration of the government assistance.
Omitted completely with zero disclosure.
Recorded in equity.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraphs 34-36: Government Assistance Disclosures
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 34 notes that government assistance may take forms which cannot reasonably have a value placed upon them (e.g. free technical or marketing advice). Such assistance is disclosed in the notes so that the financial statements are not misleading.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Group Borrowings and Subsidiary Capitalisation Rate
question: Parent Ltd. raises general borrowings at 8% and passes the funds to its subsidiary Sub Ltd. at 10% to construct a qualifying asset. In Sub Ltd.'s separate financial statements and in the group's consolidated financial statements, what interest rate is used to capitalize borrowing costs?
options: 10% in both separate and consolidated financial statements.

In Sub Ltd.'s separate financial statements, 10% (the actual borrowing cost incurred by the subsidiary); in the group's consolidated financial statements, 8% (the actual external borrowing cost incurred by the economic entity).
8% in both separate and consolidated statements.
Borrowing costs between group entities cannot be capitalized.
ref: Ind AS 23 - Group Financial Statements & Borrowing Costs
explanation: In separate financial statements, the borrowing cost to the subsidiary is its contractual cost (10%). In consolidated financial statements, intercompany interest is eliminated, and the borrowing cost capitalized cannot exceed the actual borrowing cost incurred by the group from external lenders (8%).

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Export Incentive Scrips (RoDTEP / MEIS)
question: An exporter earns Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) scrips from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) upon exporting goods. When should the government grant scrips be recognized under Ind AS 20?
options: Only when the scrips are physically utilized to clear import customs duty.
When there is reasonable assurance that the entity will comply with the conditions attached to them (export of eligible goods) and the grants will be received (assessed at the date of export).
When the scrips are sold to a third party for cash.
At the end of the financial year.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraph 7: Recognition on Reasonable Assurance
explanation: Under Ind AS 20 Paragraph 7, government grants, including non-monetary grants, shall not be recognized until there is reasonable assurance that: (a) the entity will comply with the conditions attaching to them; and (b) the grants will be received. For export incentives, recognition occurs upon completion of export performance.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 23: Exchange Rate Gains Exceeding Actual Borrowing Costs
question: An entity borrows USD at 4% interest to construct a plant. During the year, INR appreciates sharply against USD, resulting in a foreign exchange gain of ₹2 Crores. Total interest paid was ₹1.5 Crores. Can the net negative borrowing cost of ₹0.5 Crores be credited to the cost of the asset under Ind AS 23?
options: Yes, reducing asset cost below actual construction expenditures.

No, borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation cannot be negative; exchange gains can offset foreign currency interest expense up to the amount of interest incurred, and any excess exchange gain is recognized in profit or loss under Ind AS 21.
Yes, credited to revaluation reserve.
Deferred to the next financial year.
ref: Ind AS 23 & Ind AS 21: Exchange Differences as Borrowing Costs Limitation
explanation: Exchange differences are treated as borrowing costs only to the extent they are an adjustment to interest costs. An exchange gain can reduce the foreign currency borrowing cost to zero, but cannot turn the borrowing cost negative to reduce the physical cost of the asset below zero interest.

subject: Financial Reporting
tag: [ICAI CA Final FR PYQ] Ind AS 20: Presentation of Revenue Grants
question: Sun Pharma receives a ₹5 Crores government grant as an operational wage subsidy for hiring local apprentices. Under Ind AS 20, how can this grant related to income be presented in the Statement of Profit and Loss?
options: Only as a credit to Retained Earnings.
Either presented separately under 'Other Operating Income' (or 'Other Income'), or deducted in reporting the related employee benefit expense.
Must be deducted from sales turnover.
Presented in Other Comprehensive Income.
ref: Ind AS 20 - Paragraphs 29-31: Presentation of Grants Related to Income
explanation: Ind AS 20 Paragraph 29 states that grants related to income are presented as part of profit or loss, either separately or under a general heading such as 'Other Income'; alternatively, they are deducted in reporting the related expense. Both methods are regarded as acceptable.
